title: VoIP & Unified Communications
description: Design and manage voice-over-IP and unified communication networks. Tests SIP trunks, call routing, and network QoS prioritization.

seo.overviewBody: VoIP telephony powers modern business voice communications. Telephony engineers demonstrate expertise in Session Initiation Protocol (SIP), IP PBX configuration (3CX/Asterisk), Session Border Controllers (SBCs), Quality of Service (QoS) priority queuing, and IVR auto-attendants.

deliverables.title: 1. Corporate VoIP Topology & QoS Plan
deliverables.desc: Network design document detailing SIP trunking, SBC placement, and DSCP quality-of-service priority tagging.

deliverables.title: 2. IP PBX Extension & IVR Call Flow Config
deliverables.desc: PBX configuration script setting up ring groups, extension routing, voicemail-to-email, and interactive voice response (IVR) menus.

deliverables.title: 3. Call Quality & Jitter Diagnostic Report
deliverables.desc: Network analysis report diagnosing packet loss, latency, and jitter metrics affecting voice clarity.

faqs.question: Why is Quality of Service (QoS) essential for VoIP networks?
faqs.answer: Voice traffic is intolerant to delay. QoS prioritizes audio packets over general web traffic to prevent choppy calls, jitter, and dropped connections.

faqs.question: What is a Session Border Controller (SBC)?
faqs.answer: An SBC is a specialized firewall that secures SIP trunking, prevents toll fraud, and normalizes signaling between IP PBX systems and telecom providers.

faqs.question: What is the difference between SIP trunks and traditional ISDN lines?
faqs.answer: ISDN lines use legacy physical copper wire channels. SIP trunks deliver virtual voice channels dynamically over IP internet connections.
